# Human QA correction: history alpha mask

Baseline: a50b9ba4bcdc3f87eeaeced05efe03cd4869f917. After: this PR's mask-fix commit. Web Chromium captures are 1440×1000; official macOS Desktop captures are 2560×1640. Both use a task-owned memberless Channel with 32 actual committed Human messages, no model calls. Synthetic wallpaper is generated by the journey; no private media.

The previous top overlay painted native DSH's base color over the custom green body. The composer activity pseudo-element had another base-color gradient. Both are removed; only the scrollable history uses an explicit alpha mask. It fades over at most 24px at the top and 8px at the bottom, with the measured activity-overlay inset reserved when visible. Header, composer and floating controls are outside the mask. The mobile top-edge exemption is retained, but native mobile is not qualified by this run.

`e2e-message-history-mask.mjs` verifies computed mask mode, absent old overlay, unmasked composer, 32 rendered messages, real scroll to both ends, input, transparent Body over wallpaper, independent dark Body, and reload. Pixel comparison against the same rendered history with the mask temporarily disabled finds edge changes and zero changed center pixels. The temporary unmasked comparison is a diagnostic, not the before screenshot; before images come from the actual preceding code.

The native run identifies the main dsh-app window, then repeats the journey. Earlier failures were driver issues (stale Host address, unsupported message ID/patch combination, keyboard cleanup, menu focus) and an unresponsive old Desktop debug connection after rebuild; they remain private and are not accepted evidence. Only the task-owned app was restarted. No claim is made about diagnosing the old debug connection or a live working-Bot activity overlay; existing working-row/composer regressions cover that component boundary.

The paired screenshots show the same Channel, theme, colors and viewport while browsing history; exact scroll offsets may differ. See proof JSON for image-based assertions. Source tests, CI, live Web/native rendering and Human QA remain separate. Draft/unmerged; no deployment.

Focused source validation: 84 tests in six files passed (timeline, profile, composer/working rows, token and style contracts), along with build, lint, format and root/mobile types. CI is recorded separately against the published head.
